FACTS
1. This case was registered on the basis of source information against one Sh. H. R. Sapra, the then
Dy. Secretary (Alternative) (retired), Land & Building Department, Government of NCT of Delhi,
New Delhi, Sh. Swarn Singh Malhi (S.S. Malhi- Accused No.1), the then UDC/Dealing Clerk
(retired), Land & Building Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, New Delhi, Sh. Neeru Kumar
Gupta @N.K. Gupta, Advocate, (private person-A-3). Smt. Suman D/o Sh. Dharm Dev, other
unknown public servants and other unknown private persons Under Section 120-B r/w Section 419,
CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 2 of 210 420, 467, 468 & 471 IPC and Section 13(2) r/w 13
(1) (d) of P.C. Act, 1988. It is the claim of CBI that it was during the investigation of one of the Land
& Building department fraudulent recommendation cases i.e. RC 4 /2015/CBI/AC-II/ACU-7
VI/New Delhi that the original file of Land &Building Department regarding allotment of plot in the
name of one Smt. Suman was recovered from the residence of accused Sh. N. K. Gupta (Accused
No.3) during search. Consequent to verification, this recommendation was revealed as a fraudulent
one and hence, the present case was registered.
2. It is the case of CBI that Government of NCT of Delhi had launched a welfare scheme to
rehabilitate and compensate the agriculturist whose lands were acquired by the Government and
The Land & Building Department was implementing the said scheme for allotment of alternative
plots in lieu of acquired land under the scheme of "Large Scale Acquisition Development & Disposal
of Land in Delhi" announced by Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs vide letter No.
37/16/60- Delhi dated 2nd May, 1961 . In order to implement this scheme, the Land & Building
Department used to invite applications from the land owners whose lands were acquired by the
Government for grant of alternative plots through press advertisements. In case the applicant was
the recorded owner at the time of notification u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act, the following
documents were required to be submitted along with the application:
A) Revenue record , Jamabandi , Khatoni Mutation which ever is applicable.
CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 3 of 210 B) Payment certificate issued by LAC/SDM.

C)Affidavit that the applicant / dependent does not own any property in any urban area , New Delhi
, Cantt. Area.
D)Two passport sized photographs, three specimen signature , copy of election ID Card / ration card
, duly attested by gazette officer.
E) order of ADJ for compensation / probate / sale / mutation if applicable.
F) Indemnity bond registered with the Sub Registrar Delhi
3. It is the case of CBI that as per the procedure prescribed in the above said Guidelines, on receipt
of application from the applicant i.e. the owner whose land was acquired by the Government, the
contents of the application forms were verified from the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC)
concerned. The Revenue Records filed by the applicant was also verified by the Revenue staff of
Land & Building Dept. and the applicant was called for personal verification. Thereafter, the case of
the applicant was put for final consideration by the committee constituted for the purpose for
approval and for issue of recommendation to the DDA for allotment of alternative plot. The plots
were allotted by DDA through draw of lots and such allotments were based on the recommendation
letters issued by Land & Building Department in favor of allottee as per policy laid down in this
regard by the Government of Delhi.
4. It is claimed in the FIR that the above named accused criminally conspired with each other and
used forged documents to get CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 4 of 210 recommendation for allotment of a plot
measuring 80 Sq yards in the name of one Smt. Suman D/o Dharm Dev, Chirag Delhi, based on
which DDA issued allotment letter qua a plot no. 470, Sector-19, Dwarka, New Delhi measuring 67
Sq. meter to this person .It is claimed by CBI that Shri Swarn Singh Malhi , the then dealing
assistant i.e. Accused No. 1 and Shri H R Sapra , the then Under Secretary processed the application
of this person . i.e Smt. Suman and placed forged documents before the recommendation committee
which later went on to approve the recommendation for allotment of an alternative plot to her. This
plot was recommended in lieu of acquired land of Khasra no. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur vide award no.
2/90-91 dated 06.04.1990 for which compensation of Rs. 34.694.41 had been paid to the rightful
owners. It is the case of CBI that investigation revealed that the said acquired land of Khasra No
461/2 , Village Jaitpur actually belonged to one Sh. Laabh Singh and Sh. Thakar Singh, both sons of
Late Sh. Ghuma Singh who had claimed the compensation on 23.10.1991 from the government .It is
alleged by CBI that a person namely Ms. Suman had impersonated as the owner of the acquired land
in the application form submitted and she succeeded in getting the recommendation letter issued in
her name from Land and Building Department. CBI claimed that their investigation revealed that
this person Suman was a fictitious person as she was not found existing or residing at her last
reported address. As per the chargesheet, vide notification u/s 4 of LA. Act, 1984 dated 02.06.1909,
lands of village Jaitpur were notified for acquisition by Delhi Administration and plot bearing
Khasra No 461/2 was included CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025

CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 5 of 210 in the said notification. Thereafter, vide section 6
declaration dated 10.07.190- LAC was directed to take acquisition of lands notified u/s 4 of the said
Act and plot bearing khasra no. 461/2 was the included in the list of lands. The investigation of CBI
has revealed that award no 2/90-91 of acquired land of village Jaitpur was announced in the open
court on 26.04.1990 wherein the details of land owner who had claimed for compensation for their
acquired land was given .It is the case of CBI that plot no. 461/2 was in the name of Sh. Laabh Singh
and Sh. Thakar Singh, both sons of Sh. Ghuma Singh and compensation of Rs. 69308.91 in lieu of
acquisition of plot no. 461/2 was given solely to Sh. Thakar Singh on 23.10.1991 at the request of Sh.
Laabh Singh.
5. CBI has claimed that their investigation has further revealed that the farmers whose lands were
acquired by the award no. 2/90-91 could have also applied for the allotment of alternative plots as
per the above mentioned policy of Government of India . Hence as per the laid down norm by Land
& Building Department, each application was allotted a number according to the File Head Register.
In the allotted number, 32 was denoting "South Zone" and 55 was denoting "village Jaitpur". A
separate file for each application was created and submitted to the branch officer and while
submitting the application, details of the application viz name, details of acquired land, village
name, award number etc. was maintained after checking in the noting file by dealing assistant of the
branch. Thereafter, the dealing assistant would seek LAC report in a prescribed format on the
application. The CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 6 of 210 LAC report used to contain the date of notification
u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act (LA Act)-1982, name of the recorded owner of the land at the time of
publication of said notification, khasra number with area, share of the applicant, amount of
compensation with date of payment to the applicant, and date of taking of possession by the
Government. After receipt of LAC report, the file was again submitted by the dealing assistant with a
proposal to seek report from Tehsildar. L&B Dept. and Tehsildar used to submit his report with
regard to notification of land u/s 22(1) of DDA Act . On receipt of report from Tehsildar, the file was
sent to the writ cell for legal scrutiny by law officers. After obtaining legal opinion, a detailed brief of
file was prepared by the dealing clerk and it was signed by the Branch Officer for placing the same
before recommendation committee which consisted of Secretary cum Commissioner, Joint
Secretary, Law Officer and Branch Head. Once the meeting of recommendation committee was held,
the minutes of the same were drawn which contained the details of decision taken in the said
meeting. Thereafter, recommendation letter signed by Joint Secretary (Land &Building
Department) was sent to DDA for allotment of alternative plot.
6. The investigation of CBI has revealed that a meeting of the recommendation committee
consisting of Sh. R. Chandra Mohan, Secretary cum Commissioner, Smt.Asha Nayyar, Addl.
Secretary, Sh. Diwakar Singh, ALA and Sh. H. R. Sapra, Dy Secretary (Alt) was held on 15.01.1999
and in the said meeting 27 cases were placed before the committee for consideration. For each case,
separate summary sheets CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 7 of 210 had been prepared and signed after detailed
examination by the Dy. Secretary (Alt) and ALA. Based on the summary sheets and discussions, 15

cases were recommended by the committee whereas two (02) cases were recommended for
re-examination and ten (10) cases were rejected.
7. It is claimed by CBI that accused N. K. Gupta (Accused No.3) along with his wife i.e Accused No.4
Smt. Sangeeta Gupta had entered in to a criminal conspiracy with accused Saroj Bala (Accused
No.2) and dealing assistant Sh. V. K. Chauhan (deceased) both Dealing Assistants of South Zone,
Land & Building Department, GNCT of Delhi in the year 1992 and they created a false application
along with false enclosures on 29.12.1992 for allotment of alternative plot in lieu of acquisition of
land bearing Khasra no 461/2 of Village Jaitpur, Delhi which was received in the office of L& B
Department vide diary no. 7053 dated 29.12.1992. CBI has claimed that investigation has revealed
that the said application was written and signed by Accused No. 4 Sangeeta Gupta W/o Sh. N. K.
Gupta( Accused No.3) as one Suman. The application was in duplicate and was signed on
16.12.1992. In support of her claim as the applicant, accused Sangeeta(Accused No.4) had submitted
a false Nakal Jamabandi for the year 1976-77 and 1987-88 signed on 14.01.1991 & 11.10.1992
respectively and false Compensation payment certificate signed &issued on 02.12.1992 by the LAC.
The application of Smt. Suman was allotted a number F32(55)/87/92-94/LAB/Alt. It is alleged in
the chargesheet that original file of Land and Building Department CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi &
Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 8 of 210 of this application for allotment was recovered
from the residence of accused N. K. Gupta (Accused No. 3) during his house search in Case
-RC 2172015AD004/ACU-VI (i.e. RC No 4/ 2015 )a nd was a relied upon document in this case.
Thus, the aforesaid original file of Land and Building Department as recovered on house search of
Accused No.3 was obtained with permission from the Hon'ble Court for the purpose of investigation
of this case.
8. CBI has claimed that their Investigation has revealed that Sh. Thakar Singh had also applied for
the allotment of alternative plot in lieu of his acquired land comprising of land of khasra no. 461/2
on 01.01.1992 with the Land and Building Department and the file number allotted to his
application was F. 32(55)41/92-94 in the file head register of the alternative branch of L&B Dept.
Investigation by CBI revealed that in the said register, no application was given number
F.32(55)87/92-94 in the name of Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev. As per the said register, total 90
applications were received from the farmers of village Jaitpur. Investigation revealed that
application number 86 & 87 were missing from the list of applicants in the said register. The said
register was being maintained in the Alternative Branch by Dealing Assistant at the time of receipt
of application of farmers for allotment of alternative plots during the period of 1992-94 and accused
Saroj Bala( Accused No.2) was the dealing assistant at that time in the south zone of Alternative
branch. Investigation revealed that the entries in the said register pertaining to village Jaitpur were
also made by accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2) and had overwriting in them.

CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 9 of 210 Hence, it was claimed that the application bearing
number F.32(55)/87/92-94/L&B/Alt was fraudulently created by accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2
), by abusing her official position as a public servant in connivance with accused Neeru Kumar
Gupta (Accused No. 3) and accused Sangeeta Gupta Suman(Accused No.4) to cause unlawful gain to
them .
9. As per the chargesheet, accused Saroj Bala (Accused No.2) was working as a Dealing Assistant in
South Zone of Land and Building Department and hence, she was the custodian of files of south
zone bearing village code 31 to rest of the villages of south zone wherein Village Jaitpur was coded as
55. It was claimed by CBI that it was the accused Saroj Bala who had processed the application and
enclosures of applicant Suman D/o Dharam Dev and at the same time, she had also processed the
application of Sh. Thakar Singh S/o Sh. Ghuma Singh. During investigation, it was found out that
the application and enclosures of Smt. Suman were false and the same were processed by accused
Saroj Bala. The verification report viz LAC Report and Tehsildar reports (L&B) were also found to be
forged. The LAC Report shown as signed by LAC(ME) on 05.08.1994 and also shown to be issued on
11.08.1994 was also found to be forged .The said document was shown as received in Receipt Branch
of L&B Dept. on 18.08.1994 vide diary no. 5105. However, during Investigation it was revealed from
the Central Diary Register of incoming correspondences that no such report had been received on
18.08.1994 CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 10 of 210 as on this date, dairy entry started with diary no.
5659 and no LAC report was received. at diary entry 5105.
10. It was also revealed that in the file of Sh. Thakar Singh, the LAC report pertaining to his
application was signed on 05.08.1994 and issued on 11.08.1994 (at page 117). The said report was
received in Receipt branch of L&B Dept. on same day i.e. 11.08.1994 and diary number of 5565 was
also found correct as per Central Diary Register. Thus, CBI claimed that the LAC report in the case
of Smt. Suman was falsely created after receipt of LAC Report in the case of Sh. Thakar Singh in
connivance with the Accused no.2 and same was inserted by her in the file and therefore she actively
facilitated the commission of offences as she completed the false documentation by abusing her
official position and also placed it before the branch head. It was also claimed that Accused No.2
Saroj Bala being the dealing assistant had first hand knowledge of the crime as she was processing
files of both Sh. Thakar Singh and Smt. Suman for the allotment of alternative plot for the same
piece of acquired land bearing Khasra no. 461/2 at the same time and thus, her culpability in the
crime was crystal clear.
11. It is the case of CBI that in furtherance to the above said criminal conspiracy, Accused No.1 S. S.
Malhi entered into the said conspiracy with Accused No.3 N. K. Gupta and Accused No.4 Sangeeta
Gupta; who impersonated as Suman, d/o Dharamdev for fraudulent allotment of alternative plot in
her name. Accused No.1 started working in Alternative Branch from June 1997. It was found out
that the application of Suman was pending since 19.06.1995 and CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 11 of 210 on 18.06.1997, accused No.1 fraudulently and in
conspiracy with other accused initiated the note dated 18.6.1997 with a dishonest intention to get an

alternative plot allotted in the name of Suman despite the fact that she was neither the owner of the
acquired land nor had received any compensation in lieu of its acquisition. As per charge-sheet, it
was revealed that land bearing Khasra no. 461/2 was owned by Sh. Thakar Singh and Sh. Laabh
Singh and Thakar Singh had received the compensation for entire Khasra no. 461/2, Village Jaitpur
at the time of its acquisition. It was revealed that even the process for allotment of alternative plot in
lieu of acquired land of K No. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur in the name of Sh.Thakar Singh was also dealt
by Accused No.1 during the same period and in furtherance to the above said criminal conspiracy,
on 18.06.1997 Accused No.1 submitted a note before the branch head asking for approval that both
files of Suman and one Bhanu as part owners of Khasra No 461/2 , Village Jaitpur may be allowed to
be proceeded with further and the applicants may be requested to submit an affidavit with regard to
personal hearing and as a consequence thereof , Smt. Shashi Kaushal, the then Dy. Secretary (Alt.)
approved the same and a letter dated 18.06.1997 was sent to Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev in this
regard. It was found out that in furtherance of the said criminal conspiracy, after a gap of one year
I.e. on 13.07.1998, after joining of Sh. H. R. Sapra as Dy. Secretary (Alt), Accused No.1 proposed that
the applicant be asked upon to submit her affidavit regarding her personal hearing in the
department and thus, a fair letter was placed by him before Sh. H. R. Sapra. The letter was approved
on 15.07.1998 by Sh. H. R. Sapra and on 23.11.1998, CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 12 of 210 Accused No.1 put up a note to Sh. H. R. Sapra
that requisite documents have been received and the cases are complete so a fresh Check memo may
be allowed to be prepared. The same was approved by branch head on 23.11.1998. Thereafter,
accused No.1 prepared a Check memo and obtained clearance from all zones by declaring that no
older complete files were left out and no other claim in respect of same piece of land was pending in
other zones. As per the chargesheet, in the said check memo prepared by Accused No.1,he falsely
mentioned about the payment of compensation to Suman on 09.11.1992. and also showed Suman as
the recorded owner of land bearing Khasra no 461/2 at the time of notification u/s 4 of LA Act. It is
claimed by CBI that all these false details were mentioned in Check memo prepared and signed by
Accused no.1 dated 26.11.1998 and thereafter, on 27.11.1998 , he submitted a detailed note before
Sh. H. R. Sapra wherein he proposed to obtain opinion of ALA which was marked to ALA by Sh. H.
R. Sapra on 30.10.1998.
12. It is the case of CBI that Sh. Diwakar Singh, ALA had recommended for consideration of the case
before the recommendation committee as per the noting made in the file by accused No.1 and he
also suggested a time frame for obtaining response of the applicant as there was gap of more than
one year. On receipt of this ALA opinon, Sh. H. R. Sapra noted on 02.12.1998 that case file of
co-owner Bhanu linked with this file had not been seen by the ALA and Assistant may be asked to
take back the file to the ALA for his comments on the linked file. CBI has claimed that Accused No.1
in furtherance to the CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 13 of 210 said criminal conspiracy made a false declaration
on the note sheet that file of the co-owner Bhanu had been seen by ALA who had desired to put up
the linked file of Smt. Bhanu before the recommendation committee. He also suggested that both
the files of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu to be placed before the recommendation committee, which
noting was approved by Sh. H. R. Sapra on 17.12.1998. In furtherance to the said criminal
Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Swarn Singh Malhi on 8 December, 2025

conspiracy, Accused No.1 prepared a check list and summary sheet, duly signed/initialed by him for
being placed before the recommendation committee for allotment of alternative plot in the name of
Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev. It is alleged that Accused No.1 knowingly and deliberately prepared
the noting and check memo in which false details were mentioned by him and on the basis of the
said documents containing false information, the recommendation committee recommended the
allotment of the plot in the name of Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev.
13. Thus, CBI has claimed that in furtherance to the said criminal conspiracy, by working
dishonestly, knowingly and deliberately, Accused No.1 prepared the recommendation letter No.
001113 dated 19.02.1999 and initialed on the same and placed it before Sh. H. R. Sapra and got it
signed from Smt. Asha Nayar, Joint Secretary (L&B). Thereafter, the said letter was sent to the
Commissioner, Delhi Development Authority, Vikas Sadan, INA New Delhi wherein it was
requested to allot a plot measuring 80 sq. yds to Smt. Suman and by issuing this letter, Smt. Suman
had become entitled for allotment of alternative plot from DDA in her name.

CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 14 of 210
14. It is the case of CBI that Accused No.1 Sh. Swarn Singh Malhi was the custodian of the files of
South Zone, Alternative Branch, Land and Building Dept. during his tenure in said zone.
Investigation has also revealed that after issuance of recommendation letter in the name of Smt.
Suman to DDA, the file should have been consigned to Central Record Room of Land &Building
Department but the same was not done by Accused No.1 and instead the file was found in
possession of accused N. K. Gupta and his wife accused Sangeeta Gupta when the same was
recovered during their house search in RC No. 2172015A0004/ACU-Vi/ RC No 4/2015. CBI has
claimed that accused N. K. Gupta was the mastermind of this crime and he used to frequently visit
the Alternative Branch of Land and building Department to meet with accused No.1. CBI has
claimed that their investigation has revealed that the said applicant Smt. Suman was none other
than the wife of Accused No.3, i.e accused No.4 Sangeeta Gupta.
15. During investigation, the enclosures of the application of Smt. Suman which were submitted to
Land & Building Dept. were sent to CFSL with specimens of accused N. K. Gupta and accused
Sangeeta Gupta . The expert had opined that the writing in hindi on the Nakal Jamabandi were that
of accused N. K. Gupta. Hence ,CBI claimed that Accused No.3 had actively participated in
commission of the alleged offence. The accused Sangeeta Gupta W/o accused N. K Gupta was found
to be the applicant who impersonated herself as Suman D/o Dharam Dev R/o Chirag Delhi. Neither
Accused No.3 or Accused No.4 nor Suman were found to be the owners of land bearing CBI Vs.
Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.
CNR No. DLCT11-001469-2019 Page No. 15 of 210 Khasra no. 461/2 , Village Jaitpur nor any land of
Suman or Sangeeta Gupta had ever been acquired or any compensation was paid to her in lieu of the
same. However, Accused No.4 dishonestly and knowingly submitted an application in the name of
Smt. Suman dated 16.12.1992 which was shown as received in Department on the same date and all

the enclosures of the said application were false and were containing false details. During
investigation, CFSL expert had given positive incriminating opinion on the signature / handwritings
of accused Sangeeta Gupta appearing as that of "Suman" on the exhibits. It was also found out that
Accused No.4 had also provided her coloured photographs which were found attached with the said
recommendation letter No. 001113 dated 19.02.1999 sent to DDA for allotment of alternative plot in
the name of "Suman" by Land and Building Department after culmination of the meeting dated 15.1
1999. CBI has claimed that Accused No.4 impersonated herself as Smt. Suman and provided false
residential address and when DDA sent Demand Cum Allotment Letter bearing no. F. 27
[11/1999/LSB(R)/9479 dated 09.08.02 to this address, it was returned with remarks as " incomplete
address". When DDA attempted to deliver the said letter through a person, the address was found to
be non-existent and thus, it was found out that Smt. Suman D/o Dharam Dev R/o Chirag Delhi was
"non- existant".
16. Sh. H. R. Sapra, the then Deputy Director of Land and Building Department was named as an
accused in the FIR. CBI has claimed that investigation revealed that he had worked as Dy.

Department for the period 1997 to June, 1999 and when he joined the Alternative Branch, Accused
No.1 was the dealing assistant of the south zone of the branch and he was the one dealing with the
file of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu which was already in process in the section. It was revealed that
the verification had already been completed by accused Saroj Bala and accused S S Malhi. It was on
18.06.1997 that the last note-sheet entry asking for approval that both files may be allowed to be
proceeded with further and the applicants may be requested to submit affidavit in current date
regarding their personal hearing was filed, which was approved by Smt. Shashi Kaushal, Dy
Secretary (Alt). On joining of Sh. H R. Sapra, Accused No.1 again put up a fair letter asking
applicants to submit requisite documents/information. The noting of Accused No. 1 was routed
through Sh. Brinda Ban Gupta, Office Supt. on 17.07.1998 and Sh. H. R. Sapra approved the same
on that very date. Thereafter, accused no.1 submitted to Sh. H. R. Sapra that requisite documents
had been received and now cases were complete and a fresh check memo be allowed to be prepared.
This noting was approved by Sh. H. R. Sapra on 23.11.1998 and thereafter, Accused No.1 prepared a
check memo under his signature dated 26.11.1998 and thereafter it was certified on 14.01.1999, one
day prior to scheduled meeting of recommendation committee that no older complete file was left
out. It was after preparation of check memo dated 26.11.1998 that Accused No.1 also prepared
detailed note in the note sheet on 27.11.1998 and put it up before Sh. H. R. Sapra for obtaining ALA
report. Accordingly. Sh. H. R. Sapra marked the file to ALA on CBI Vs. Swarn Singh Malhi & Ors.

receipt of file from ALA, Sh. H. R. Sapra noted on 02.12.1998 that the case file of the co - owner
linked with this file had not been seen by the ALA. He marked the file to Dealing Assistant (AD) that
DA may please take back the file to the ALA for his comments on the linked file. On this, on
03.12.1990, Accused No.1 made a false declaration on the note sheet that file of co-owner had been
seen by ALA claiming that he desired to put up the linked file of Smt. Bhanu before the

recommendation committee. It is alleged that thereafter, Accused No.1 suggested that both the files
of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu be placed before the recommendation committee and Sh. H. R.
Sapra approved the same on 17.12.1998. Thereafter, the both cases of Smt. Suman and Smt. Bhanu
were recommended in the meeting of recommendation committee held 15.01.1999.CBI has claimed

handwriting expert testimony wherein they rejected the notion that handwriting expert evidence
should be treated with inherent suspicion or requires mandatory corroboration in all cases. The
judgment clarified that a handwriting expert is "no accomplice" and their testimony should not be
automatically condemned to a lower class of evidence. While doing so the Court acknowledged that

and there was no reliable contradictory evidence, uncorroborated testimony may be accepted. The
Court emphasized that an expert's opinion should be tested by the acceptability of the reasons given
by him rather than being viewed with initial suspicion. The Apex court held that -
"Expert testimony is made relevant by Section 45 of the Evidence Act and where the
Court has to form an opinion upon a point as to identity of handwriting, the opinion

made a relevant fact...So, corroboration may not invariably be insisted upon before
acting on the opinion of an handwriting expert and there need be no initial suspicion.

137. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court had observed in the case of Runu Ghosh Vs. CBI (Crl. Appeal No.
482/2002 , decided on 21.12.2011) with respect to provisions of Sec. 13(1) (d) (iii) of PC Act that
what was vital to the prosecution to prove its case was to establish that the actions of the public
servant and decisions which resulted in a third party obtaining a pecuniary advantage or valuable
thing were done without public interest. When a public servant's decision exhibits manifest
disregard to the interest of the public resulting in pecuniary advantage or vesting of a valuable thing
with a third party, liability for criminal misconduct arises qua the said public servant u/s. 13 (1) (d)
(iii) of PC Act. This provision does not require proof of intent as the only act made punishable by the
Parliament is act done against public interest. Thus, the applicability of Sec. 13 (2) of PC Act which

public servant does not depend on the fact of the public servant having obtained a pecuniary
advance or valuable thing for himself. The ingredients of the Section 13(1)(d) are attracted if the
public servant by his action causes a third party to obtain an advantage by harming the public
interest. Public servants are obliged to act in a manner which is fair, just and equitable as they hold
the property of the State in their hands for general welfare of the public by acting as trustees of the
same. The level of trust reposed in public servants by the society must be reflected in their high
standards of behavior and the same is expected out of them in discharge of their official duties as
well. Hence, an action of a public servant exhibiting disregard to the public interest with
corresponding result of unlawful gain to a third party is to be necessarily construed as an act of
criminal misconduct by the said public servant.

140. Sec. 415 of IPC defines cheating as whoever by deceiving any person, fraudulently or

set to cheat that person. The explanation of this section provides that a dishonest concealment of
facts is a deception within the meaning of this section.

situations in which no transfer of property has been occasioned by the said deception. In the case of
